# FixedNat

An unsigned integer of fixed capacity, holding no storage of its own.

```rux
pub struct FixedNat {
    // private fields
}
```

`Copy`, and 520 bytes wide, so it is passed by reference rather than by value everywhere in this package. The
limbs are least significant first and `length` counts the ones in use, so zero is `length == 0` and there are
never leading zero limbs above it — every operation restores that before it returns.

<h3 id="multiply-add-small"><code>MultiplyAddSmall</code></h3>

```rux
pub func MultiplyAddSmall(
    self: &var FixedNat,
    factor: uint64,
    addend: uint64
) -> bool
```

Multiplies by `factor` and adds `addend`, in one pass over the limbs.
The pair is one operation because that is how a digit is absorbed while reading a number, and doing it in
two passes would double the work for no gain.
Answers false when the product needs more limbs than the capacity holds, leaving the value exactly as it
was — a caller that sees this has passed the bound Docs/NarrowFloat.md proves is not reached.

| Name     | Type     | Description            |
| -------- | -------- | ---------------------- |
| `factor` | `uint64` | what to multiply by    |
| `addend` | `uint64` | what to add afterwards |

**Returns**: true when the result fits

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Format/Src/FixedNat.rux#L184)

<h3 id="subtract"><code>Subtract</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Subtract(self: &var FixedNat, other: &FixedNat)
```

Subtracts `other`, which must not be larger than this value.
The caller establishes `other <= self` first, by [`Compare`](/docs/api/format/fixed-nat#compare) or by construction. Subtracting a larger value
has no answer in an unsigned type, and this borrows past the top rather than reporting it.

| Name    | Type        | Description      |
| ------- | ----------- | ---------------- |
| `other` | `&FixedNat` | what to subtract |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Format/Src/FixedNat.rux#L275)

<h3 id="multiply-power-of-ten"><code>MultiplyPowerOfTen</code></h3>

```rux
pub func MultiplyPowerOfTen(
    self: &var FixedNat,
    power: uint
) -> bool
```

Multiplies by ten to the `power`.
Done as one pass per limb-sized chunk of the power rather than one per digit: ten to the nineteenth is the
largest power of ten a `uint64` holds, so a power of three hundred and twenty-four costs seventeen passes
instead of three hundred and twenty-four.
Answers false when the result does not fit. A power applied in chunks stops at the chunk that does not fit,
so the value is left part-scaled rather than untouched — the one place in this file where that is so, and
it is reached only past a bound that is proved not to be.

| Name    | Type   | Description           |
| ------- | ------ | --------------------- |
| `power` | `uint` | the exponent to apply |

**Returns**: true when the result fits

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Format/Src/FixedNat.rux#L305)

## Related

<h3 id="fixed-nat-limbs"><code>FixedNatLimbs</code></h3>

```rux
pub const FixedNatLimbs: uint = 64;
```

How many sixty-four-bit limbs a [`FixedNat`](/docs/api/format/fixed-nat) holds.
Sixty-four, which is 4,096 bits: the 3,681 the narrow conversion reaches at worst, and 415 bits of headroom
over it. See Docs/NarrowFloat.md for where the 3,681 comes from.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Format/Src/FixedNat.rux#L28)
